dedupe_keys.name: high resolution ai data centre training workloads dataset york university

description: This dataset records the electrical and computing behaviour of artificial intelligence training jobs at sub-second resolution, to support modelling of how AI data centres draw power from the grid. It contains 32 training sessions on NVIDIA H100 and B200 eight-GPU server nodes and 40 sessions on consumer NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 machines, more than 1.8 million samples in all, each with total power demand, CPU and GPU utilisation, per-GPU power, memory use and temperatures, for tasks such as forecasting, classification, reinforcement learning and text and image generation. It was produced at York University in Toronto and described in Scientific Data in 2026, with technical validation of timing, hardware limits and cross-metric consistency. Coverage: single machines and single eight-GPU nodes, not whole facilities; sampling every 20 ms from Python monitoring and about 100 ms from HWiNFO. Format and access: CSV files in three folders on figshare, with training and monitoring code on GitHub; free of charge under CC BY 4.0 on figshare (the article itself is CC BY-NC-ND). Caveats: node-level measurements must be scaled up with assumptions about cooling, networking and job mix; hardware and software versions will age quickly. Simulation uses: building load profiles of AI data centres for grid connection and capacity planning, stress tests of power systems against fast load swings, and digital-twin models of facility power. Related records: the NLR generative AI workload power profiles cover a supercomputer, the EPRI data centre load projections give totals, and Alibaba and Google cluster traces give job mixes.
